refined_claim_text: ReCAAP ISC Annual Report 2025 (covering January–December 2025, published January 2026) reports that armed robbery incidents in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) rose 74% — from 62 incidents in 2024 to 108 incidents in 2025 — the highest recorded in SOMS during the 19-year period 2007–2025. Total piracy and armed robbery incidents across Asia reached 132 in 2025, a 23% increase over 107 incidents in 2024.

primary_sources_found.key_data: 108 incidents in SOMS in 2025; 74% increase over 62 incidents in SOMS in 2024; 19-year high for SOMS; 132 total Asia incidents; 23% overall increase vs 2024

Full annual report confirms: 132 total Asia incidents (+23% vs 2024), SOMS 108 incidents (+74% vs 62 in 2024), 82% of Asia incidents were in SOMS. SOMS incidents declined sharply from Aug–Dec 2025 after Indonesian arrests.
2024 Annual Report confirms 107 total Asia incidents in 2024 (baseline year for the 2025 comparison). SOMS had 62 incidents in 2024.

notes: The original claim (PP-40) accurately cites the 74%/108-incident figures but contains two imprecisions that require correction: (1) Geography: The 74% rise and 108-incident count apply specifically to the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS), not all of Southeast Asia. Total Asia-wide incidents were 132 (up 23% from 107 in 2024). (2) Report year: The figures come from the ReCAAP ISC Annual Report 2025 (data year 2025, published January 2026), not a '2025 report covering 2024 data.' The 2024 Annual Report (data year 2024) showed 107 total Asia incidents and 62 SOMS incidents. Canonical report URL: https://www.recaap.org/reports. Direct PDF: https://www.recaap.org/resources/ck/files/reports/annual/ReCAAP%20ISC%20Annual%20Report%202025.pdf. Both PDFs verified via markitdown. Source is an intergovernmental body (ASEAN-affiliated, Singapore-based) — qualifies as primary/authoritative. Confidence upgraded to H. Claim is weakened only in the sense that geographic scope needed narrowing from 'Southeast Asia' to 'Straits of Malacca and Singapore'; the specific figures are confirmed correct.
